investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" on the 2 eligible nodes and node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the required node affinity/selector for remote agent pods. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, no remote agent pod can be scheduled. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion at the VM slot level, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the probe in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs calls createAgent with machineType "remote" (line 1885), which triggers pod creation that immediately stalls unscheduled, preventing any evidence from being written back to the check result.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=154898, pod was stuck unscheduled for 148s before the check timed out as fail.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe never reaching the VM-assignment step.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no partial evidence was written, confirming the runner did not progress past pod scheduling.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 144s, no evidence keys collected.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 142s, no evidence keys collected.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which is the code path that submits the pod requiring kata.peerpods.io/vm.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never schedules.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: existing remote agent VMs are consuming all available slots and have not been released, leaving zero capacity for new pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall.
Tertiary — VM lifecycle leak: remote agent VMs from prior eval runs or user sessions may not have been cleaned up, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots indefinitely and starving new scheduling attempts.
Quaternary — cluster under-provisioning: the 2 affinity-eligible nodes may have been provisioned with a kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity that is too small for concurrent eval and production workloads.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl or the cluster API shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available (allocatable > used) on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling constraint must be investigated.

If a new remote agent pod schedules and reaches running state immediately after the eval failure timestamp, the exhaustion was transient and may have been caused by a brief spike rather than a sustained leak.

If the 2 affinity-eligible nodes show zero kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity (i.e., the resource is not configured at all on those nodes), the root cause is a node configuration or labeling error rather than slot exhaustion.
If re-running the eval immediately after this report produces a passing result with all 4 evidence keys present, the condition was self-resolving and not a persistent capacity problem.

If only remote-agent-create fails while remote-agent-state or remote-agent-runtime passes in a subsequent run, the failure is not uniformly infrastructure-level and a per-check code or timing difference should be investigated.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on affinity-eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing slot exhaustion as a distinct check status rather than a scheduling timeout.

Add a VM slot leak detection eval that counts pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm requests older than a configurable TTL and fails if any are found, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust capacity.

Add a node affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold, alerting on topology shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.

Refine the remote-agent-create eval to distinguish between scheduler-rejected (Unschedulable) and application-layer failures by capturing the scheduler event reason as a separate evidence key, enabling more precise triage in future failures.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Production Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-31T12:58–13:03Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm (production-api environment) has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no VM slot was available for any of the three eval-provisioned pods. The pods remained Unschedulable for 142–148 seconds before the eval timed out, preventing createAgent (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) from completing and leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) unpopulated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent workloads or prior eval runs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving none for new probe pods. Supported directly by the scheduler message in failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, and sibling.remote-agent-runtime.

Node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's required node affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes were recently reconfigured or their labels changed, capacity would appear to drop even if total VM slots are unchanged.

Insufficient total kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity provisioned for the cluster: the cluster may have been sized for a lower concurrent remote-agent load than is now being exercised by evals plus production workloads.

A node or VM pool scaling event (scale-down, node eviction, or maintenance) reduced available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots at the time of the eval run. No direct evidence of this is present but it is consistent with the timing.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl or the cluster dashboard shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are available and not exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, resource exhaustion is not the cause and node affinity/selector misconfiguration becomes the primary hypothesis.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after freeing VM slots succeeds and returns all required evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), this confirms the exhaustion hypothesis and rules out a code or configuration regression in the eval runner.

If the node affinity/selector on the pod spec was recently changed so that it no longer matches any node with kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, the root cause would be a scheduling configuration change rather than raw capacity exhaustion.

If other non-remote-agent workloads are also failing to schedule on the same cluster at the same time, the issue may be broader than the kata.peerpods.io/vm pool (e.g., a node outage or cluster-wide resource pressure).

If the eval runner's createAgent function has a bug introduced by a recent change that causes it to request an incorrect resource or node selector, the scheduler error could be a symptom of a misconfigured pod spec rather than true capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that probes kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on the production cluster and warns when available slots fall below a safe threshold (e.g., fewer than 2 free slots).

Add a pre-scheduling health check eval that verifies at least one node matching the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector has a free kata.peerpods.io/vm slot before the full remote-agent-create/state/runtime eval sequence runs.

Add a pod-scheduling latency eval that fires a warning if a remote-agent pod takes longer than a configurable threshold (e.g., 30s) to transition from Pending to Running, catching capacity pressure before it causes full eval timeouts.

Add a cluster node-label consistency eval that asserts the expected number of nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and match the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector, catching label drift before it reduces the schedulable pool.

With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request times out unscheduled (~142–148 s), preventing agent creation and causing all downstream evidence collection to fail. investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" on the 2 eligible nodes and node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the schedulable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that match the required node affinity/selector for remote agent pods. With 0 of 6 nodes available and preemption unable to free capacity, no remote agent pod can be scheduled. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion at the VM slot level, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the probe in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs calls createAgent with machineType "remote" (line 1885), which triggers pod creation that immediately stalls unscheduled, preventing any evidence from being written back to the check result.
proof: failed-check.message: scheduler message explicitly states '0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=154898, pod was stuck unscheduled for 148s before the check timed out as fail.
expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 4 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) are absent, consistent with the probe never reaching the VM-assignment step.
failed-check.evidence: evidence object is empty ({}) — no partial evidence was written, confirming the runner did not progress past pod scheduling.
sibling.remote-agent-state: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 144s, no evidence keys collected.
sibling.remote-agent-runtime: identical scheduler error, pod stuck 142s, no evidence keys collected.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1877-1885: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1885, which is the code path that submits the pod requiring kata.peerpods.io/vm.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:250-258: contract requires vmIdPresent=true and remoteState oneOf [running, idle, ready] — neither assertion can be evaluated when the pod never schedules.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots exhausted on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes: existing remote agent VMs are consuming all available slots and have not been released, leaving zero capacity for new pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: 4 of 6 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall.
Tertiary — VM lifecycle leak: remote agent VMs from prior eval runs or user sessions may not have been cleaned up, holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots indefinitely and starving new scheduling attempts.
Quaternary — cluster under-provisioning: the 2 affinity-eligible nodes may have been provisioned with a kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity that is too small for concurrent eval and production workloads.

This is an eval-layer infrastructure failure; no evidence of user-traffic or incident signals is present in the packet, so treat this as an observability eval outage until cluster-level investigation confirms or denies broader impact.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl or the cluster API shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots available (allocatable > used) on the 2 affinity-eligible nodes, resource exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling constraint must be investigated.

If a new remote agent pod schedules and reaches running state immediately after the eval failure timestamp, the exhaustion was transient and may have been caused by a brief spike rather than a sustained leak.

If the 2 affinity-eligible nodes show zero kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity (i.e., the resource is not configured at all on those nodes), the root cause is a node configuration or labeling error rather than slot exhaustion.
If re-running the eval immediately after this report produces a passing result with all 4 evidence keys present, the condition was self-resolving and not a persistent capacity problem.

If only remote-agent-create fails while remote-agent-state or remote-agent-runtime passes in a subsequent run, the failure is not uniformly infrastructure-level and a per-check code or timing difference should be investigated.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used capacity on affinity-eligible nodes before attempting remote agent creation, surfacing slot exhaustion as a distinct check status rather than a scheduling timeout.

Add a VM slot leak detection eval that counts pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm requests older than a configurable TTL and fails if any are found, catching cleanup failures before they exhaust capacity.

Add a node affinity coverage eval that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold, alerting on topology shrinkage before it causes scheduling failures.

Refine the remote-agent-create eval to distinguish between scheduler-rejected (Unschedulable) and application-layer failures by capturing the scheduler event reason as a separate evidence key, enabling more precise triage in future failures.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-31T12:58–13:03Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could never be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm (production-api environment) has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the 2 eligible nodes. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that no VM slot was available for any of the three eval-provisioned pods. The pods remained Unschedulable for 142–148 seconds before the eval timed out, preventing createAgent (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) from completing and leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) unpopulated. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-31 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval pod because 2 nodes had insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, and no evidence (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was returned to satisfy the remote-agent-runtime expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that support peer-pod VMs. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod request times out unscheduled (~142–148 s), preventing agent creation and causing all downstream evidence collection to fail. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the evidence; this is an eval-infrastructure failure.
proof: failed-check.message: 'pod stuck unscheduled for 142s (Unschedulable): 0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector. preemption: 0/6 nodes are available: 2 No preemption victims found for incoming pod, 4 Preemption is not helpful for scheduling.'

sibling.remote-agent-state: same Unschedulable / Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm message, latencyMs=151284, endedAt=2026-07-31T13:00:40.105Z
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=146088, status=fail — eval timed out well before the 420000 ms outage threshold, confirming the pod never scheduled

expected-output.missing-required-evidence: all 5 required evidence keys (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent — consistent with createAgent never returning (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918, line 1918: 'const agent = await createAgent(args, track, "remote", null, orgId)')
expected-output.contract: assertion 'message containsIgnoreCase hello from aura' could not be evaluated because message evidence was never produced

source.infra/evals/status/features.json:185: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false, so this failure does not by itself trigger a feature outage, but remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true (lines 183–184) and both siblings also failed
possibleCauses: Primary: kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes is fully consumed by existing workloads or leaked/stuck pods, leaving no capacity for new eval pods.

Secondary: The node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to only the 2 peer-pod nodes; if those nodes are saturated there is no fallback, and preemption found no victims to evict.

Tertiary: A prior eval run's remote-agent pod(s) were not cleaned up (withCleanup in run-status-probes.mjs line 1916 may have failed), holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots and preventing new pods from scheduling.

Lower probability: The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit on the 2 capable nodes was reduced (e.g., by a node configuration change), shrinking available capacity below what concurrent eval runs require.

reproductionSteps.label: Re-run only the remote-agent-runtime eval probe against production-api
reproductionSteps.details: Use the same environment variables as the scheduled observability workflow to reproduce the scheduling failure.

reproductionSteps.label: Inspect current kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable and used capacity on all 6 cluster nodes
reproductionSteps.details: Confirm whether the resource is fully consumed on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes.

reproductionSteps.label: List all pods currently holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources to identify leaks or stuck pods
reproductionSteps.command: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].resources.requests["kata.peerpods.io/vm"] != null) | {name: .metadata.name, namespace: .metadata.namespace, phase: .status.phase}'
reproductionSteps.details: Identify any pods from prior eval runs that were not cleaned up and are holding VM slots.

reproductionSteps.label: Check the node affinity and node selector on the remote-agent pod spec
reproductionSteps.details: Confirm that the pod is restricted to only the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes and has no fallback scheduling path.

reproductionSteps.label: Run all three sibling checks together to confirm the shared scheduling failure
reproductionSteps.details: All three checks should reproduce the same Unschedulable message if the root cause is cluster-wide VM resource exhaustion.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agent pod scheduling — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on production-api cluster nodes
affectedAreas.reason: The scheduler message in failed-check.message and both sibling check messages explicitly names 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2 of 6 nodes as the blocking constraint.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-runtime eval check
affectedAreas.reason: The eval runner branch at lines 1913–1918 calls createAgent with type 'remote', which requires a schedulable kata peer-pod VM. Pod scheduling failure prevents createAgent from returning, leaving all required evidence absent.

affectedAreas.label: remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state eval checks (required=true siblings)
affectedAreas.reason: Both required sibling checks failed with the same Unschedulable message (sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state). Per features.json lines 183–184 these are required=true; per line 187 degradedAfterFailures=1, so the remote-agents feature is in a degraded state in the eval system.

affectedAreas.label: Remote Agents feature — eval health status
affectedAreas.reason: All three checks under the remote-agents feature failed. With degradedAfterFailures=1 and outageAfterFailures=2 (lines 187–188), and two required checks failing, the feature's eval health status will reflect degraded or outage depending on aggregation logic.

recommendedNextActions: Inspect kata.peerpods.io/vm resource usage on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes immediately to determine current capacity vs. demand.
Identify and terminate any stuck or leaked remote-agent pods from prior eval runs that may be holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without active workloads.

If resource exhaustion is confirmed, either increase the kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on existing nodes, add additional peer-pod-capable nodes to the cluster, or reduce the number of concurrent remote-agent eval runs.
Review the withCleanup logic in infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs to ensure remote-agent pods are reliably terminated after each eval run, including on failure paths.
After restoring capacity, re-run all three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) to confirm recovery.

Note: remote-agent-runtime is registered as required=false (infra/evals/status/features.json line 185), but remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true (lines 183–184); the two required checks failing is the higher-severity signal to resolve.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Re-run the remote-agent-runtime eval probe to confirm the failure is reproducible
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Directly reproduces the failing eval and confirms whether the scheduling constraint persists. A pass would indicate the issue was transient.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Check kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. used on all cluster nodes
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms whether the resource is fully consumed on the 2 peer-pod-capable nodes, proving or disproving the resource exhaustion hypothesis.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: List pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources to detect leaked eval pods
recommendedVerifierProbes.command: kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].resources.requests["kata.peerpods.io/vm"] != null) | {name: .metadata.name, namespace: .metadata.namespace, phase: .status.phase}'
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Identifies whether prior eval runs left pods running that are consuming VM slots and preventing new scheduling.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Inspect node labels on all 6 nodes to verify peer-pod affinity configuration
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: Confirms that exactly 2 nodes carry the label required by the remote-agent pod's node affinity/selector, and that the other 4 nodes are correctly or incorrectly excluded.

recommendedVerifierProbes.label: Run all three remote-agent sibling checks together to confirm shared infrastructure failure
recommendedVerifierProbes.reason: If all three reproduce the same Unschedulable message, it confirms the failure is a shared cluster-level constraint rather than an isolated eval runner issue.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is available and not exhausted on the 2 peer-pod nodes, the root cause is not resource exhaustion and the node affinity/selector mismatch or a different scheduling constraint would need investigation.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and produces all 5 required evidence keys, the failure was transient (e.g., a brief capacity spike) rather than a sustained resource exhaustion.

If the 4 non-peer-pod nodes are shown to have been incorrectly excluded by a misconfigured node affinity (e.g., a label was removed), the primary cause would be a node labeling or affinity configuration error rather than VM resource exhaustion.
If no stuck or leaked pods are found holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources, the exhaustion is due to legitimate concurrent workloads rather than a cleanup failure in withCleanup.
followUpEvals: Add a pre-flight eval that checks kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. requested capacity on all peer-pod-capable nodes before attempting remote-agent creation, surfacing resource exhaustion as a distinct 'capacity' failure rather than a scheduling timeout.

Add an eval that verifies no orphaned remote-agent pods are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources after each eval run cycle, catching cleanup failures in withCleanup before they exhaust cluster capacity.
Add a node-affinity/selector validation eval that confirms the expected number of nodes match the remote-agent pod's scheduling requirements, catching label drift or misconfiguration early.

Consider adding a latency-bucketed eval that distinguishes 'pod never scheduled' (0 evidence, scheduling error message) from 'pod scheduled but agent failed to start' to make triage faster in future incidents.
